notes.def-cherednik:
Definition — Cherednik operators $C_i$ and $\tilde C_i$
- $C_i$ is assembled from $R_{i,j}$ together with the shift $q^{D_i}$; $\tilde C_i$ is the variant normalised by $1/x_i$.
- $N=2$ relations, eq. (51) of the paper:
$$\tilde C_2=\frac{1}{x_2}C_2,\qquad \tilde C_1=\frac{1}{x_1}C_1+\left[\frac{1}{x_1},\,C_2\right].$$
- Verified exactly by symbolic simplification, not merely at sample points: $[C_1,C_2]=0$ and $[\tilde C_1,\tilde C_2]=0$.
- Verified: $C_1+C_2$ and $C_1C_2$ both preserve the space of symmetric functions, so they descend to commuting operators on it.
- Warning: eq. (52) of the paper reuses the symbol $C_i$ for a different object. See the notation-trap card before quoting either relation.
notes.def-dim:
Definition — the DIM algebra and its $N$-body representation
- $U_{q,t}(\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_1)$, the elliptic Hall algebra: a $q$-deformed $W_{1+\infty}$ whose commutative families produce integrable many-body systems.
- Parameter convention used throughout this map: $(q_1,q_2,q_3)=(q,t^{-1},q^{-1}t)$ with $q_1q_2q_3=1$.
- Generative relation at the level of modes:
$$x^+(z)\,x^-(w)\sim\frac{(1-qz/w)\,(1-t^{-1}z/w)}{(1-q^{-1}z/w)\,(1-tz/w)}\;x^-(w)\,x^+(z).$$
- The $N$-body representation acts on functions of $x_1,\dots,x_N$; the symmetric functions form a stable subspace for the operators used here.
- Reading order: this card gives the algebra; the ray and Cherednik cards give the operators whose commutativity is the point of the paper.
notes.def-macdonald:
Definition — Macdonald operators $D_1, D_2, D_3$
- $D_1$ is the Ruijsenaars–Schneider Hamiltonian; the $D_k$ are its commuting higher partners.
- At $N=2$, with $A_1=\dfrac{tx_1-x_2}{x_1-x_2}$ and $A_2=\dfrac{tx_2-x_1}{x_2-x_1}$:
$$D_1=A_1\,q^{D_1}+A_2\,q^{D_2}.$$
- Eigenfunctions: the symmetric Macdonald polynomials $M_\lambda$.
- Verified eigenvalue checks: $D_1M_{(1,0)}=(1+qt)M_{(1,0)}$, $D_1M_{(1,1)}=q(1+t)M_{(1,1)}$, and $D_1M_{(2,0)}=(1+q^2t)M_{(2,0)}$ with $c=\dfrac{(1-t)(1+q)}{1-qt}$.
- Verified: $[D_1,D_2]=0$, and eqs. (45) and (47) of the paper reproduce $D_1,D_2,D_3$ from the expansion of $\log D(z)$.
notes.def-rays:
Definition — rays $(a,b)$ and word operators $W^{(r)}_i$
- A ray is a pair $(a,b)$. The ray $(0,1)$ carries the Macdonald operators $D_k$; the ray $(-1,r)$ carries the operators $S_{(-1,r)}$ and their word-level building blocks $W^{(r)}_i$.
- Construction rule that matters in code: a word of length $r$ uses exactly $r$ factors of $C$ and $r-1$ factors of $x$. Getting this count wrong silently changes the operator.
- Verified: $[W^{(1)}_1,W^{(1)}_2]=0$, and likewise for word lengths 2, 3 and 4 — the families attached to one ray commute.
- Verified: $[D_1,S_{(-1,2)}]\neq 0$, so different rays give genuinely different families rather than the same one relabelled.
- Reading: the paper's "commutative families" are indexed by rays.
notes.def-roperator:
Definition — $R$-operators and the $RLL$ relation
- $R_{i,j}$ acts on the $i$-th and $j$-th coordinate only; at $N=2$ the only one that occurs is $R_{1,2}$.
- Verified intertwining property: $q^{D_1}s_{1,2}=s_{1,2}q^{D_2}$, so $R$ exchanges the two shifts.
- Verified: $R_{1,2}R^{-1}_{1,2}=\operatorname{Id}$ and $R^{-1}_{1,2}R_{1,2}=\operatorname{Id}$.
- Verified: $R^2\neq\operatorname{Id}$ in this normalisation. Do not treat $R$ as a permutation or an involution.
- Role: $R$ is the ingredient from which the Cherednik operators are assembled, and the reason those operators commute.

notes.eq-d12:
The $N=2$ dictionary between Cherednik and Macdonald operators
- Matching the coefficients of $u$ and $u^2$ in the factorisation above gives
$$t\,(C_1+C_2)=D_1,\qquad t^2\,C_1C_2=D_2.$$
- Verified symbolically on symmetric functions.
- Practical value: it converts every statement about the Cherednik operators into a statement about the Macdonald operators and back, which is what makes the paper's two families comparable.
- Normalisation caveat: the coefficients are exactly $t$ and $t^2$ only in the normalisation of this paper. A different normalisation of $C_i$ shifts them, so re-derive before reuse.
notes.eq-du:
Factorisation of $D(u)$ — the central identity of the reconstruction
$$D(u)=\prod_i\left(1+u\,t^{N-1}C_i\right)\;\overset{N=2}{=}\;(1+utC_1)(1+utC_2)=1+uD_1+u^2D_2.$$
- Reading: the generating function of the Macdonald operators is a product of linear factors in the Cherednik operators.
- Verified at $N=2$: expanding the product reproduces exactly $1+uD_1+u^2D_2$ on symmetric functions.
- Consequence: commutativity of the $D_k$ is inherited from commutativity of the $C_i$, so one exact check at $N=2$ explains the whole mechanism.
- Scope caveat: verified at $N=2$ only. The statement for general $N$ is taken from the paper and has not been re-derived here.
notes.eq-eq60:
eq. (60) — factorisation of the $(-1,2)$ ray operator
- The factorised right-hand side of eq. (60) agrees with
$$\sum_i \tilde C_i\,x_i\,\tilde C_i$$
up to the overall constant $\dfrac{t^2(q-1)^2}{q^2}$.
- Verified: after restriction to symmetric functions no residual $s_{1,2}$ remains, so the naive symbolic form is safe once one works on symmetric inputs.
- Verified: the restricted operator is a combination of $q^{2D_1}$, $q^{2D_2}$ and $q^{D_1+D_2}$ with constant coefficients.
- Placement: this is the $r=2$ member of the $(-1,r)$ ray, so it sits at the boundary between the ray construction and the Macdonald operators.
notes.ex-blocks:
$N=2$ building blocks — the worked layer of this map
- Primitives: $q^{D_i}$ acts as $x_i\mapsto qx_i$ on the $i$-th coordinate; $s_{1,2}$ swaps $x_1\leftrightarrow x_2$.
- Verified relations: $A_1+A_2=t+1$; $[D_1,s_{1,2}]=0$; $x_1s_{1,2}=s_{1,2}x_2$; $D_2=t\,q^{D_1+D_2}$.
- Intuition: at $N=2$ everything is generated by one swap and two elementary shifts, which is small enough that each identity can be checked in closed form.
- Use: this card is the entry point for reproducing the whole chain — the later cards only quote relations that already exist at this size.
notes.lem-degree:
Lemma — $S_{(-1,2)}$ lowers the total degree by exactly one
- Verified: for each symmetric polynomial tested, applying $S_{(-1,2)}$ reduces the total degree by exactly 1.
- Two explicit values:
$$S_{(-1,2)}(1)=\frac{x_1+x_2}{t^2\,x_1x_2},\qquad S_{(-1,2)}(x_1x_2)=\frac{q^2(x_1+x_2)}{t^2}.$$
- Verified: $x_1x_2$ is not an eigenfunction of $S_{(-1,2)}$ — the operator moves degree layers instead of preserving them.
- Reading: $S_{(-1,2)}$ is a lowering operator on the graded ring of symmetric functions, not a symmetry of it. Contrast this with $D_1$ and $D_2$, which are diagonalisable on the same space.
notes.lem-rinv:
Lemma — $R$ is invertible but is not an involution
- Verified: $R_{1,2}R^{-1}_{1,2}=\operatorname{Id}$ and $R^{-1}_{1,2}R_{1,2}=\operatorname{Id}$.
- Verified: $R^2\neq\operatorname{Id}$ in the normalisation used by the paper.
- Consequence for verification code: never assume $R^{-1}=R$ and never auto-simplify $R^2$ to the identity; both directions must be carried explicitly.
- Consequence for the algebra: traces and squares built from $R$ may not be simplified as if $R$ were a permutation operator.

notes.ref-paper:
Mironov–Morozov–Popolitov 2024 · Commutative families in DIM algebra, integrable many-body systems and $q,t$ matrix models
- arXiv: 2406.16688v2 | Local PDF: /Users/andylyu/Zotero/storage/C7QQ9C7Y/
- Role in this map: the primary source. Section 6 defines the $N$-body representation of the DIM algebra and the family of commuting operators built from it.
- Claims used downstream: eqs. (42)–(47) (Macdonald operators), eqs. (51)–(52) (Cherednik operators in two normalisations), eq. (60) (factorisation of the $(-1,2)$ ray operator).
- Defect found while reading: the same letter $C_i$ denotes two different operators in Section 6 — see the notation-trap card.
- Status: partially checked. Only the $N=2$ layer has been verified symbolically.
notes.rem-eq52:
Notation trap — $C_i$ in eq. (52) is not the $C_i$ of Section 6.2.3
- The paper uses one letter for two different operators. Equation (52) silently redefines $C_i:=x_i\tilde C_i$.
- Verified at $N=2$, the discrepancy in the first operator is
$$x_1\tilde C_1-C_1=\left(\frac{1}{t}-1\right)s_{1,2}\,q^{D_1}.$$
- Verified: the difference does not vanish when restricted to symmetric functions, so this is a genuine change of operator and not a harmless abuse of notation.
- Action taken here: every verification label in the harness names which of the two objects it means. Anyone reading eq. (52) on its own should do the same.
notes.rem-numeric:
Remark — how identities were tested
- Deterministic symbolic simplification alone is not reliable once $s_{1,2}$ is present in the expression.
- Procedure: cancel the difference, then substitute three independent rational values of $q,t,x_1,x_2$.
- All three results zero ⇒ accepted as an identity; any non-zero result ⇒ rejected.
- Limitation, stated plainly: three points is evidence and not proof. Wherever a purely symbolic argument is available it was used instead, and those cases are exact — $[C_1,C_2]=0$, $[D_1,D_2]=0$ and the $D(u)$ expansion were all confirmed symbolically.
notes.res-45:
Result — verification status of the reconstruction
- 45 / 45 checks pass, reproducibly.
- Independently reconfirmed here: the $D(u)$ factorisation; the $t$ and $t^2$ dictionary; the split between the two objects called $C_i$; the constant in eq. (60); the degree-lowering property of $S_{(-1,2)}$; and $RR^{-1}=\operatorname{Id}$ with $R^2\neq\operatorname{Id}$.
- Not verified: any statement at $N>2$; the $q,t$ matrix-model side of the paper; the general elliptic $D(u)$ beyond the $N=2$ trace identity.
- Consequence for use: the $N=2$ layer can be quoted with confidence, the rest must be quoted as the paper's statement rather than as a checked result.
notes.task-verify:
Task — the symbolic verification harness
- Artefact: verify_nbody_N2.py (SymPy). 45 checks grouped by object: building blocks, $R$ and Cherednik operators, the ray $(0,1)$, the ray $(-1,r)$, and the $N=1$ limit.
- Result: 45 checks, 45 passed, 0 failed. Re-running the script on a separate interpreter reproduced the recorded output line for line.
- Implementation rule 1: an operator power must be iterated $k$ times. Writing it as an ordinary scalar power produces false failures.
- Implementation rule 2: expressions containing $s_{1,2}$ can defeat symbolic simplification — fall back to the numeric procedure on the next card.
- Acceptance rule used: a difference is accepted as zero only when it is zero at all three sample points.
